Subject: Finovia post-demo: latency targets, streaming needs & mutual action plan

Hi Emily / Jonathan —

Thanks again for the demo time today. Quick recap and asks so we can turn the conversation into a scoped PoC: we focused on your primary performance constraints (live transcript streaming + summary generation) and sketched some targets. Please confirm the numbers below or flag changes.

Finovia SLO summary (requested by product):
- Interactive typing / live transcript start latency: p50 < 100 ms, p90 < 300 ms
- Streaming per-token start latency: goal < 50 ms for first token, sustained < 70 ms
- Long-form generation (summaries): p50 < 200 ms, p90 < 600 ms for 2k token responses
- Throughput: baseline 1,200 reqs/min; burst up to 3,000 reqs/min for scheduled reports
- Concurrency: steady 80 concurrent sessions, peak 200 concurrent sessions during day-end batch
- Token throughput: ~1.5M tokens/hr during peak windows

Questions / clarifications we need from you:
1) Are the concurrency numbers above per-region or global?
2) Will transcript streaming always be single-turn (append-only) or will you require frequent re-roll to the start of conversation (affects KV cache strategy)?
3) Can you share recent production traces or a 24-hour sample of request rate (CSV attached is fine)?
4) What SLAs / error budget trade-offs are acceptable during PoC? (e.g., 99% p90 vs 95%)

Proposed next steps / Mutual Action Plan (MAP):
- MAP-1 (Week 0): Finalize SLOs & sample traces (Finovia) — target by 2026-10-08
- MAP-2 (Week 1-2): 2-week PoC on Redwood Dedicated (prelim config below) — tentative start 2026-10-12
- MAP-3: Performance acceptance tests, runbook + guardrails (Redwood + Finovia) — complete by end of PoC
- MAP-4: Pricing / commit discussion and DocuSign SOW (commercial) — during PoC week 2

Prelim PoC config (for scoping only):
- Model variant: smaller streaming-optimized open model + low-latency quantized variant for summaries
- Hardware: 2x A10G (or equivalent) with pinned KV cache nodes for session affinity
- Autoscale policy: maintain concurrency headroom (scale at 70% concurrency usage)
- Batching: adaptive short-window batching for small transcripts; continuous batching for summaries

Attachments: priya_demo_slo_checklist.xlsx (SLO table + test plan), redwood_poC_playbook.pdf (PoC runbook).

If these SLOs look right, we'll send a formal PoC SOW + timeline. Would you prefer a short call tomorrow morning (30 minutes) to sign off the MAP?

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Thanks Priya — this is very clear and helpful. A few answers and a note from our infra team:

- Concurrency: numbers are global for our initial rollout (we may shard by region later)
- Streaming behavior: mostly append-only, but we do occasionally rewind the last ~30s for corrections (so KV cache should support small-window rewinds)
- Traces: attaching a 24-hour sample export (finovia_perf_history.csv) — includes request timestamps and basic payload sizes
- Error budget: we can tolerate 95% p90 during PoC but need a clear path to 99% for GA

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you confirm network egress assumptions (we operate behind a strict firewall and route via our VPC)?
- For the streaming start latency, we need worst-case first-token under 150 ms on our side — if Redwood can meet p90 < 150 ms during PoC we'll consider that acceptable.

We are ok with a 2-week PoC starting 10/12. Jonathan and I will review the SOW once you send it.

Thanks,

Quick internal scoping note (copying Emily/Jonathan so they see our approach):

Based on Finovia’s answers, here’s a proposed technical plan for the 2-week PoC and a very high-level cost/size estimate to align expectations:

PoC objectives (success criteria):
- Demonstrate streaming-first-token p90 <= 150 ms on Finovia traces
- Sustained concurrency handling of 80 sessions with spike to 200 without >1% increase in p90
- End-to-end throughput target: 1,200 reqs/min steady with a 3k reqs/min burst
- Acceptance threshold: 95% p90 during PoC, with monitoring flags for regressions to 99% as next milestone

Technical approach:
- Use 2x A10G nodes + 1 KV cache node; prefer colocated (same AZ) to minimize network hops
- Model: streaming-optimized decoder with micro-batching window of 10-20 ms for transcripts
- Cache: session affinity + 30s rewind window to support corrections
- Fallback: automatic fallback to smaller model variant on load spike (graceful degradation)

Estimate (very rough):
- Infra: $X/day for Dedicated nodes (will provide an itemized estimate in SOW)
- Engineering time: ~2 engineer-weeks for integration + tracing hooks + acceptance tests

Immediate MAP items I can own:
- Prepare PoC SOW & cost estimate (Rishi) — deliver 2026-10-07
- Provision preliminary Dedicated pool & run synthetic smoke tests (Laura + infra) — target 2026-10-11
- Provide a smoke-test checklist and dashboard links for Finovia (Karthik) — target 2026-10-09

Attaching our PoC playbook for Emily/Jonathan to review. Once we have sign-off on SLO numbers we’ll lock config and schedule the provisioning window.

—Rishi

Adding technical acceptance criteria and a short runbook for the PoC. I attached the SLO checklist (priay_demo_slo_checklist.xlsx) — please review and confirm. Key items below: 

Acceptance test plan (high level):
- Ingest Finovia trace (sanitized) and run 24-hour replay against PoC environment
- Measure: first-token latency, per-token jitter, model latency for 2k token summaries, and end-to-end error rate
- Run 3 controlled spike tests (x2, x3 of baseline) and validate graceful degradation and fallback correctness
- Validate session rewind with 30s window without cache corruption

Runbook highlights:
1) Smoke test script (Karthik): start with 50 concurrent streams for 15 minutes, record p50/p90
2) Escalation: if p90 degrades by >25% vs baseline, auto-scale policy triggers and notification to Redwood eng on-call
3) Data handling: use Finovia-sanitized traces only; no retention beyond PoC without signed agreement

Owner assignments: 
- Smoke tests + traces: Karthik Iyer
- Provisioning + infra checks: Laura Bennett
- Commercial SOW + pricing: Rishi Malhotra
- Customer coordination + acceptance sign-off: Priya Natarajan

Please confirm the owners and we’ll add these items to the hubspot MAP.

Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
